subject: sci
source: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science (0653) syllabus for examination in 2025–2027 and 2028–2029 (topics B1–B16, C1–C12, P1–P5) — Cambridge International; Year 11 completes the course and revises for the May/June exams

weeks.topic: Chemistry: preparation of salts
objectives: Prepare a soluble salt from an acid and an insoluble base
Describe filtration and crystallisation

weeks.topic: Physics: general properties of waves
objectives: Describe transverse and longitudinal waves
Use v = fλ
Describe reflection, refraction and diffraction of water waves

weeks.topic: Biology: gas exchange in humans
objectives: Describe the features of gas exchange surfaces
Explain ventilation of the lungs
Compare inspired and expired air

weeks.topic: Chemistry: arrangement of the Periodic Table and Group I
objectives: Describe groups and periods
Describe the reactions of Group I metals with water and predict trends

weeks.topic: Physics: reflection and refraction of light
objectives: Apply the law of reflection
Describe refraction and total internal reflection

weeks.topic: Biology: aerobic and anaerobic respiration
objectives: State equations for aerobic and anaerobic respiration
Describe uses of energy in the body

weeks.topic: Chemistry: Group VII, transition elements and noble gases
objectives: Describe halogen properties and displacement reactions
Describe properties of transition elements and noble gases

weeks.topic: Physics: thin converging lens and dispersion of light
objectives: Draw ray diagrams for a converging lens
Describe dispersion of white light by a prism

weeks.topic: Biology: drugs
objectives: Define a drug
Describe the use of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance

weeks.topic: Physics: the electromagnetic spectrum and sound
objectives: Describe the regions, uses and hazards of the EM spectrum
Describe sound as a longitudinal wave and relate pitch and loudness to frequency and amplitude

weeks.topic: Chemistry: properties and uses of metals and alloys
objectives: Compare properties of metals and non-metals
Explain the uses of alloys such as brass and stainless steel

weeks.topic: Biology: sexual reproduction in plants
objectives: Identify parts of a flower
Describe pollination, fertilisation and germination conditions

weeks.topic: Chemistry: reactivity series, corrosion and extraction of metals
objectives: Order metals by reactivity
Describe rusting and its prevention
Relate extraction method to reactivity

weeks.topic: Biology: sexual reproduction in humans
objectives: Identify parts of the male and female reproductive systems
Describe fertilisation and the role of the placenta

weeks.topic: Review: waves, gas exchange, respiration, the Periodic Table, metals and reproduction
objectives: Revisit term 1 Year 11 topics across all three sciences
Practise mixed-science exam questions

weeks.topic: Physics: electrical charge, current and voltage
objectives: Describe charge and current
Measure current and potential difference in circuits

weeks.topic: Physics: resistance, electrical energy and power
objectives: Use R = V/I
Calculate electrical power and energy

weeks.topic: Chemistry: water, air quality and climate
objectives: Describe tests for water and water treatment
Describe air pollutants and the greenhouse effect

weeks.topic: Physics: circuit diagrams, series and parallel circuits
objectives: Draw circuit diagrams with standard symbols
Compare current and p.d. in series and parallel circuits

weeks.topic: Biology: energy flow, food chains, food webs and the carbon cycle
objectives: Construct food chains and webs
Describe energy flow between trophic levels
Describe the carbon cycle

weeks.topic: Chemistry: fuels, alkanes and alkenes
objectives: Describe fractional distillation of petroleum
Compare alkanes and alkenes
Test for alkenes with bromine water

weeks.topic: Physics: electrical safety, cells, generators and motors
objectives: Explain fuses and earthing
Describe how generators and motors work

weeks.topic: Chemistry: polymers
objectives: Describe addition polymerisation
Discuss environmental problems of plastics

weeks.topic: Biology: human influences on ecosystems — habitat destruction and conservation
objectives: Describe causes and effects of habitat destruction
Explain conservation methods

weeks.topic: Chemistry: chromatography, separation and identification of ions and gases
objectives: Carry out paper chromatography and calculate Rf values
Choose separation techniques
Identify common gases and ions

weeks.topic: Physics: space physics — the Solar System, stars and the Universe
objectives: Describe the Solar System and orbits
Describe the life cycle of stars
Describe galaxies and the expanding Universe

weeks.topic: Mock exams: full combined science syllabus
objectives: Complete full-length mock papers under exam conditions
Use mock feedback to build a revision plan

weeks.topic: Review: biology B1–B9 (organisms, cells, nutrition and transport)
objectives: Revise cells, enzymes, nutrition and transport
Practise biology data questions

weeks.topic: Review: biology B10–B16 (disease, respiration, reproduction and ecology)
objectives: Revise immunity, respiration and reproduction
Practise ecology and human-impact questions

weeks.topic: Review: chemistry C1–C6 (particles, bonding, stoichiometry and reactions)
objectives: Revise bonding and equations
Practise rate and energy questions

weeks.topic: Review: chemistry C7–C12 (acids, Periodic Table, metals, environment, organic, analysis)
objectives: Revise salts, group trends and metals
Practise organic and chemical test questions

weeks.topic: Review: physics P1–P2 (motion, forces, energy and thermal physics)
objectives: Practise motion and energy calculations
Revise thermal energy transfer

weeks.topic: Review: physics P3–P5 (waves, electricity and space) and practical skills
objectives: Practise wave and circuit calculations
Plan experiments and analyse data

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: multiple choice paper (Paper 1 or 2)
objectives: Answer multiple-choice questions across all three sciences
Manage time and use elimination

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: theory paper (Paper 3 or 4)
objectives: Answer structured biology, chemistry and physics questions
Use correct units, equations and scientific terms

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: practical or alternative to practical paper (Paper 5 or 6)
objectives: Plan investigations and identify variables
Record results and draw conclusions

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: final exam window and course reflection
objectives: Complete any remaining exam papers
Reflect on the course and choose next steps in the sciences
